messages:
Sam: quick sync — we need to define the delegated-token surface for third-party integrations. current API keys are everywhere and painful to rotate.
Lina: agreed. are we leaning toward opaque bearer tokens + introspection, or signed JWTs validated locally? both have ops tradeoffs.
Ravi: op cost: introspection adds latency and a dependency, but JWTs force us into fast key rotation and jwks distribution.
Marta: also think about claim granularity. do we encode project_id + role in the token or keep tokens minimal and resolve roles via an internal mapping service?
Sam: proposal: two token flavors: (A) short-lived signed JWTs with project_id and scopes for external integrators, validated via cached JWKS at the edge; (B) long-lived opaque project keys for infra-only paths, but with strict admin flags + telemetry.
Lina: for (A) what TTL are we thinking? 5-15 minutes? shorter TTLs reduce window for abuse but increase mint rate.
Ravi: 10m seems reasonable. we can rate-limit mint per client id. also require token mint to include a source IP or key-handle for PoP on high-priv tokens.
Marta: mapping: edge validates JWT signature, extracts project_id and scope, then consults a local role-mapper cache (in-memory) to get effective RBAC roles. the role-mapper updates via stream when policies change.
Sam: yes — avoid sync calls on the fast path. role-mapper should have clear semantics: if unknown project -> deny and emit audit with reason=unknown_project.
Lina: migration question — lots of services accept legacy keys. we should add an "allow_legacy" feature flag per route and emit a deprecation warning header for responses when legacy key used.
Ravi: migrate plan: (1) measure usage and owners; (2) flip allow_legacy=false in canary; (3) owners get 90d deprecation window; (4) auto-disable after expiry unless owner requests extension.
Marta: revocation model — for JWTs rely on short TTLs + key rotation. for compromised long-lived keys, maintain a revocation list checked at authorizer startup refresh (not per-request). revocations should be pushed to caches via pub/sub quickly.
Sam: security controls: broker must require authenticated client cert or service principal to mint tokens; high-priv scopes need PoP (ECDSA signed handle). audit every mint + include requestor principal in token "iss" claim.
Lina: also add mint quotas and anomaly detection: sudden spike in mints from a principal -> alert + auto-throttle.
Ravi: edge caching details: cache jwks for 1h but support key rotation with KID header. on verification failure, edge should attempt an async jwks refresh and fail closed for the single request.
Marta: tests: include race-case where project created but role-mapper lags — define a short grace window (30s) for newly-provisioned projects to avoid flapping during onboarding. must be audit-only during canary.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: authz-role-mapper v1.3 -> canary rollout scheduled on infra-cluster-2 at 2026-04-02T04:00Z.
Sam: OK i'll draft an RFC skeleton: token flavors, mint broker spec, jwks/rotation, role-mapper contract, legacy-key migration, telemetry+alerts. tagging Lina/Ravi/Marta to own sections.
Lina: i'll take telemetry + deprecation UX.
Ravi: i'll write the broker threat model + PoP design.
Marta: i'll draft role-mapper API + streaming contract.
Sam: thanks — if no objections i'll open the RFC PR end of day.
